stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta for $2.7B — Its Third CX AI Deal in Two Weeks
stories.body: On November 2, 2026, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, a Stanford AI Lab spinout whose voice agents run complex customer calls end-to-end and also coach human reps in real time, for a reported $2.7 billion. The deal — Salesforce's third CX acquisition in two weeks after its $3.6B Fin (formerly Intercom) pickup — will fold Cresta into Service Cloud while Cresta keeps supporting existing contact-center and telephony platforms. Named enterprise customers running Cresta voice agents include Marriott, Comcast, and Alaska Airlines.
stories.why: Cresta is a named competitor and Salesforce is rapidly assembling an end-to-end AI CX stack (Fin for chat/email, Cresta for voice, Informatica for data). A seller must be ready to answer 'why not just buy the Salesforce bundle?' — the answer is integration risk, Salesforce's own acknowledgment that agents still need a governed context layer underneath, and the lack of retail-specific domain ontologies in any of these acquisitions.
stories.source_label: AI Weekly / The Information (via Aragon Research)

stories.title: BCG 'Are CPG Companies Ready for Agentic Commerce?' — 59% Report No Meaningful Capabilities (Oct 30, 2026)
stories.body: BCG's GenAI CPG Survey 2026 finds that 59% of US CPG companies report no meaningful agentic AI capabilities today, even as 80% of US consumers use AI and nearly half already shop with it. BCG's parallel retail survey of 150 retailers and brands (Oct 21) found that 68% of retailers expect agentic commerce to have a significant or transformational effect within two years, yet 24% have not moved beyond the assessment stage. BCG's analysis also shows that scaling the full set of AI initiatives across the demand value chain can deliver 220–350 basis points of cumulative EBIT for CPGs and 180–360 bps for retailers.
stories.why: This is the sharpest recent proof point that the gap between AI ambition and production deployment is structural, not just budgetary — and BCG ties it directly to data and agent-readiness gaps in CPG and retail. Sellers can use these figures to frame why a context/knowledge layer must precede any agentic rollout, and to put urgency on the 59% who are exposed.

stories.title: Sierra and Meta Launch 'Personal Agent Protocol' — An Open Standard for Agent-to-Business Communication (Oct 6, 2026)
stories.body: At Sierra Summit in San Francisco on October 6, 2026, Sierra and Meta announced the Personal Agent Protocol (PAP), an open standard governing how personal AI agents communicate with businesses; Stripe, Shopify, Walmart, and Genesys are listed as launch partners. Sierra said it will publish the v0.1 specification and hold design workshops later in October. The 2026 Summit also introduced Tandem Voice, new models, and updates separate from the eight products launched at Sierra Summit 2025 — which included Agent Studio 2.0 and the Agent Data Platform.
stories.why: PAP is an infrastructure commitment, not a feature: it sets the protocol layer through which consumer AI agents (Alexa, Gemini, ChatGPT) will talk to enterprise commerce and service systems. If this standard takes hold, every enterprise retailer will need a machine-readable, governed data layer behind it — exactly the context and ontology problem Graas solves. Sellers should ask prospects whether their product catalog, pricing, and policy data are structured well enough to respond to an external agent query today.

stories.title: Onix Whitepaper: 'The Semantic Layer Is Not Enough' — Agents Need a Four-Layer Context Stack (Oct 2026)
stories.body: Research across 522 enterprise queries cited by Onix found that agents with unified, multi-dimensional context achieved 38% higher accuracy than agents relying on semantic definitions alone. Onix argues that every successful production AI deployment in 2026 requires four components working together: a knowledge graph for entity and relationship mapping with lineage, a governed semantic layer for metric definitions, a retrieval layer for unstructured content, and a governance infrastructure that makes every AI output traceable to its source data. Onix's Wingspan 2.0 platform is built around what it calls a 'Semantic Twin' as shared infrastructure, so each successive agent starts with a richer foundation rather than rebuilding context from scratch.
stories.why: This is a direct, citable rebuttal to prospects who believe standing up a BI semantic layer is sufficient before deploying agents. The 38% accuracy delta is a sales-ready proof point showing why incomplete context stalls pilots, and the four-layer stack mirrors the architecture conversation Graas has with enterprise retail and CPG accounts.

stories.title: Parloa CPG Case: Decathlon's AI Agent Handles 500K+ Interactions/Year, Identifies 74% of Customers by Order Number
stories.body: Parloa's published CPG use-case data shows that Decathlon's deployed AI agent handles more than 500,000 customer interactions per year, identifies 74% of customers automatically by order number, and has eliminated 20% of repetitive tasks previously handled by human agents. A separate ATU deployment on the same platform booked one in three appointments autonomously, cut staff phone time by 60%, and went live in six weeks. Parloa positions CPG and retail AI agents as deployable alongside existing OMS, CRM, and ERP systems without requiring a full platform migration.
stories.why: These are named enterprise outcomes — resolution rate, identification rate, and time-to-live — from a retail/CPG context, making them directly usable on a sales call as proof that agents in real workflows produce measurable cost-to-serve reductions. The 'deploy alongside existing systems' framing is also a direct counter to the objection that an enterprise must replace its stack before getting value.
